messages:
Sam: hey team — Sam here, first day! trying to get my first branch pipeline green but hitting auth errors when the Buildkite job tries to push the image to GHCR. who should I bug for CI perms?

Buildkite Bot: build #42 failed on step `publish-image` (exit code 1)
```
> Pushing to ghcr.io/redwood-inference/sam-demo:branch-7a1c
> denied: requested access to the resource is denied
> failed to push some refs to 'ghcr.io/redwood-inference/sam-demo'
```

Sam: also saw a GHA check complaining `403` earlier in the PR checks, not sure if that's related. pasted my pipeline env below: 
```
env:
  DOCKER_REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  DOCKER_USERNAME: sam
  DOCKER_PASSWORD: ${GHCR_PAT}
```

Jamie: welcome! :wave: easiest path is usually the org-level GitHub App for Buildkite or a PAT with `write:packages` (packages scope) — GH's `GITHUB_TOKEN` from actions often can't push to GHCR unless you explicitly enable package permissions. are you using the org GitHub App or a PAT in the pipeline?

Sam: using a PAT that I generated during onboarding (thought that would be fine). I used `repo` + `workflow` scopes but didn't add `packages`. doh.

Mira: onboarding checklist note: we have a doc with exact scopes for CI PATs and the preferred flow (org GitHub App). https://internal.redwood.ai/onboarding/ci-auth — but tl;dr: for Buildkite image pushes to GHCR we recommend either
- GitHub App installed on the repo/org with `packages: write`, or
- PAT with `write:packages` + `read:packages` (not just repo/workflow).

Sanjay: another gotcha — if you're using the GH App approach, the app needs to be granted access to the repo _and_ to packages. For PATs, make sure the token is stored in Buildkite as a secure env var and not expired. If you want, I can temporarily add you to the ci-team on GitHub so you can test.

Sam: thanks — would appreciate that. for now, is there an easy local test to confirm the PAT scope before re-running Buildkite?

Jamie: yes — locally run:
```
echo "$GHCR_PAT" | docker login ghcr.io -u <your-username> --password-stdin
docker push ghcr.io/<org>/<repo>:test
```
if that errors with `denied` you need `write:packages`. Also `gh auth status` can show whether your gh CLI is using the same creds.

Sam: ran the `docker login` test and got the same `denied` response. looks like scope issue. will regen PAT with packages scope.

Mira: once you regen, drop the new token into Buildkite as `GHCR_PAT` in the pipeline settings (or ask infra to set it for the repo pipeline). ping me and I can kick off a re-run.

Sam: new token created and replaced in the pipeline env. requeued the Buildkite build. fingers crossed. :crossed_fingers:

Buildkite Bot: build #43 started — step `publish-image`

Buildkite Bot: build #43 succeeded :tada: — image pushed to ghcr.io/redwood-inference/sam-demo:branch-7a1c

Sam: woohoo, thanks everyone! tagging this thread in my onboarding notes. cc @Mira @Jamie for perms walkthrough later. :smile:
